scope: Only approved-root host-path capture depth handling, its immediate reference callsites, and source-guard/write ordering in the two external retainers.

findings.problem: Native result artifact refs are joined to output before requiring that each ref is relative to that exact native output. An absolute ref to an ordinary-named private file elsewhere inside PROJECT replaces the output prefix. capture() then accepts it because its containment check is only PROJECT-wide, so that file can be captured and published even though it is outside the declared native public corpus.
findings.minimal_fix: Validate each row.ref as a nonabsolute component-safe relative host reference before joining, and require the resulting path to remain relative to output before calling capture. This can avoid the cloud depth limit while retaining a narrower source boundary than PROJECT.
findings.minimal_regression: Use a mocked protected reader and a synthetic absolute PROJECT/private-sentinel/product.json reference; require refusal before the reader is called. Keep the real deep ordinary public-file success case. No real private file needs to be created or read.

safe_delta_observations: For already allowlisted host paths, relative_to(approved_root) followed by safe_component on every retained component rejects outside-root paths and parent traversal before the protected reader is called.

Calling artifact_bytes(path.parent, path.name) avoids applying the cloud eight-component limit to the whole host-relative path. It still invokes the same bounded opened-file kernel reader, which checks all actual ancestors and rejects linked/reparse aliases and non-single-link files. No cloud policy or product source is changed.

CapturedEvidence retains one raw snapshot per path and refuses differing bytes on recapture; expected commitments are checked against those same bytes. Current retainer source/package guards remain before tracked evidence writes, so the capture change does not move those guards after publication.

The historical retainer explicitly maps actual PASS to PASS assertions and actual FAIL to NOT_RUN assertions, requires the recorded execution's reaping and guards, and gives full software qualification credit NONE. This is historical attribution rather than a new current-source guard claim.
limits: No retainer, test, publication, native process, qualification, active/runtime evidence, database/auth/config content, provider or network was executed or accessed. This is not a full retainer re-audit or acceptance review. The hashes identify the inspected pre-repair snapshots.
